SLIP is a stitch pattern that provides texture to both sides of the knitting. Commonly slip is used "wrong-side facing", but often both sides are beautiful. Slip can also be combined with stripes creating amazing fabric.
Depending on your machine, there may be a single setting or left/right settings available

To pass the carriage across the bed without knitting or dropping stitches depends on the correct carriage settings and the needle positions.
Some machines have buttons to push in, others have knobs or levers.
Slip means to knit only the stitches in D-E-F (middle and hold positions) and NOT knit the stitches in B (working) position.

What can you do with the slip setting on your machine?

  • Add Texture
    Slipping stitches carries strands across the PURL SIDE of the knitting, creating interesting texture.
  • Add Color
    Slipping stitches extends stitches of opposite colors across subsequent rows.
  • Construction:
    • Marker Rows
    • I-Cord
    • Textured Stripes with Slip
    • Single Row Stripes of color
    • Pintuck (ribber)
    • Free Pass
    • Slip Cast On

blocks.title: What can you do with Slip Stitch on Your Machine?

components.html: Because the strands are carried across the purl side of the work, the obvious choice for the "right side" (public side) of the knitting is the purl side. But this versatile stitch has more uses!

Before you start

How do you set your machine to slip?
What are your "plain knitting" settings?
This 10 minute exercise will go a long way towards UNDERSTANDING slip on YOUR machine
TIP: Remove the sinker plate from your carriage and observe the action of the needles
Work Exercises 1-4 with NO YARN
1
Exercise #1 - plain knitting
  1. No yarn in the carriage
  2. Pull 20 needles to "D" Position
  3. Carriage Set for Plain Knitting
  4. Push carriage from right to left.  What Happens?
  5. Push carriage from left to right.  What Happens?

Watch (feel) as the needles are engaged and return to working position

2
Exercise #2 - Free Pass
  1. No yarn in the carriage
  2. Pull 20 needles to "B" (working) Position
  3. Engage slip levers/buttons
  4. Push carriage from right to left.  What Happens?
  5. Push carriage from left to right.  What Happens?

Needles remain in working position.
If your machine has right and left slip buttons/ levers, repeat this exercise engaging them separately.
NOTE: Singer SK840 will not "free pass" using the slip setting. "Pop" the carriage with the release lever to free pass

3
Exercise #3 - Slip Individual needles - The basis of slip stitch
  1. No yarn in the carriage
  2. Position 20 needles in "B" Position
  3. Using the 1x1 needle pusher, pull every other needle to "D" position
  4. Set the BOTH Slip Levers / Buttons
  5. Push carriage from right to left.  What Happens to the needles in D position?
  6. Push carriage from left to right. Does anything change?

All Needles are returned to working position.
If your machine has right and left slip buttons/ levers, repeat this exercise engaging them separately.

4
Exercise #4 - Slip groups of needles - The basis of Slip Stitch patterns
  1. No yarn in the carriage
  2. Position 20 needles in "B" Position
  3. Pull sets of 3 needles to "D" position
  4. Disengage the LEFT Slip Lever/Button
  5. Engage the RIGHT Slip Lever/Button
  6. Push carriage from right to left.  What Happens to the needles in D position?
  7. Pull sets of 3 needles to "D" position
  8. Push carriage from left to right. What happens?

All Needles are returned to working position.
If your machine has right and left slip buttons/ levers, repeat this exercise engaging them separately.

Before you start

Did you try these exercises WITHOUT Yarn?
It is important that you can visualize (and feel) how the slip settings control the needles.
This 30 minute exercise will go a long way towards UNDERSTANDING slip on YOUR machine
TIP: Repeat the previous exercises WITH YARN
5
Exercise #5 - plain knitting
  1. Cast on 20 stitches and knit a few rows (add weights if needed)
  2. Pull 20 needles to "D" Position
  3. Carriage Set for Plain Knitting
  4. Push carriage from right to left.  What Happens?
  5. Pull 20 needles to "D" Position
  6. Push carriage from left to right.  What Happens?
All stitches will knit and the needles will be returned to working position. The concept of the "plain knitting setting" is important to remember. Create a "plain knitting" reference card and keep it near your machine.

6
Exercise #6 - Free Pass
  1. With the knitting on the machine and stitches in the needles
  2. 20 stitches in work and in "B" (working) Position
  3. Engage slip levers/buttons
  4. Push carriage from right to left.  What Happens?
  5. Push carriage from left to right.  What Happens?
Needles remain in working position, but the stitches WILL NOT knit
NOTE: Singer SK840 will not "free pass" using the slip setting. "Pop" the carriage with the release lever to free pass

7
Exercise #7 - Slip Individual needles - The basis of slip stitch
  1. Position 20 needles in "B" Position
  2. Using the 1x1 needle pusher, pull every other needle to "D" position
  3. Set the BOTH Slip Levers / Buttons
  4. Push carriage from right to left.  What Happens to the needles in D position?
  5. Push carriage from left to right. Does anything change?
Needles in "D" will knit and Needles in "B" will slip. Note the slip strands UNDER the needles.All Needles are returned to working position.
If your machine has right and left slip buttons/ levers, repeat this exercise engaging them separately.

8
Exercise #8 - Slip groups of needles - The basis of Slip Stitch patterns
  1. No yarn in the carriage
  2. Position 20 needles in "B" Position
  3. Pull sets of 3 needles to "D" position
  4. Disengage the LEFT Slip Lever/Button
  5. Engage the RIGHT Slip Lever/Button
  6. Push carriage from right to left.  What Happens to the needles in D position?
  7. Pull every 4th needle to "D" position
  8. Push carriage from left to right. What happens?
All Needles are returned to working position.
the groups of 3 needles in "B" slip and a 3 stitch float is formed UNDER the needels. If your machine has right and left slip buttons/ levers, repeat this exercise engaging them separately.

To keep the edges from getting distorted and to make seaming easier, pay attention to what needles are being selected. You don't want to slip the very edge needles.

From Wikipedia
In jacquard fabric, the pattern and colors are incorporated into the weave instead of being printed or dyed onto the surface of the fabric. The term "jacquard" indicates how the pattern is woven, not the specific pattern itself.
As machine knitters, we tend associate "jacquard" with double bed jacquard (DBJ) and overlook other ways of creating multi-color fabrics on our machines.
  • Fairisle (stranded knitting)
  • Multi-color tuck
  • Multi-color slip
  • Knit-weave
  • Plaiting

In this example, we used a very simple stitch pattern.
This is stitch #325 from the Stitch World III book. (20 stitches x 12 rows)

DAK STP File
The advantage of multi-color slip is fewer floats. Looking at this stitch pattern, you can see that if this was stranded with fairisle, there would be floats as long as 6 stitches.
In 2 color slip, each row is knit with multiple passes of the carriage, employing the slip settings on your machine. Although it can be done without a color changer, (swapping the colors as needed), a color changer makes fast work of this technique.
For every 2 rows there are 4 passes of the carriage:
Rows 1 and 2:
  • Color 1 (purple) - pass 1 and 2 - the white needles are slipped and the working needles are knit with purple
  • Color 2 (white) - pass 3 and 4 - the purple needles are slipped and the previously slipped needles are knit with white
This process is repeated to create the pattern, reducing the floats.

There are many models of color changers available for the different machines.
The buttons and setup may be different from this Brother color changer, but the concept is the same.
Remember, if you don't have a color changer, you can still work multi-color slip by simply swapping out the colors manually.

Slip Cast on- Extra FAST!
This may not be the prettiest cast on method, but it's closed and FAST.
Consider it for knitting swatches or any time you use a Scrap and Ravel Cast On method.
Slipped Edge Stitch Technique Although this is technically not a slip stitch technique (it uses the hold setting), this technique can add a beautiful chain edge to your knitting.

You just ripped out a row of knitting or you put some knitting back on the bed from the garter bar or you did a bit of shaping and now your carriage is on the opposite side of the working yarn.
Positioning the carriage is an essential skill for machine knitters.

Here are 4 ways to "free pass"; getting the carriage to the same side as the working yarn without knitting or dropping stitches.

1Remove the carriage

Sure, you could take the carriage off the machine, run to the other end and replace the carriage ... but that's a "rookie move". Take control of your machine and use the carriage settings.

2Use the hold setting

2 steps:
  1. Put all needles in hold position
  2. Set the carriage to hold
When you pass the carriage, the needles will not move and stitches will not drop or knit.

3Use the slip setting

With many machines, the slip setting will also allow for a free pass.
  1. The stitches are in the hooks of the needles
  2. The needles are in working position
  3. The carriage is set to slip
When you pass the carriage, the needles will not move and stitches will not drop or knit.

4"Pop" the carriage (Silver Reed/ Singer/Studio machines)

Pop the carriage (silver machines). Use the release lever and raise the top section of the carriage.
The carriage will pass across without knitting or dropping stitches.

Don't forget to reset your row counter after a free pass.

I-cord (or slip cord) can be used in many ways to embellish your knitting.
It can be used as shoulder straps for girls dresses, belts and decorative ties … the list is endless!
Machine knitters can quickly make I-cord and it is an essential technique for beginners to learn.

23
Exercise #23 - Experiment with I-Cord
  1. Typically knitters knit I-cord over 3 needles.
    • Cast on over 3 needles
    • Set the carriage to slip in one direction
    • Knit a few inches of I-Cord
  2. Cast on over 4 needles
    • Set the carriage to slip in one direction
    • Knit a few inches of I-Cord
  3. Cast on over 5 needles
    • Set the carriage to slip in one direction
    • Knit a few inches of I-Cord
  4. Often knitters will rely on the natural curl of the knitting instead of using slip.
    • Cancel Slip
    • Knit a few inches of plain knitting over 3-5 needles
Compare each section of cord.
Which method do you prefer?
Use slip for a beautiful, tubular, ribbed cast on
In order to work these techniques, be sure to know how to slip with your ribber.

Add texture with full needle rib by working slip on the main bed (controlled by punchcard or electronics) WITH ribber stitches in work at the same time.
On Japanese machines, the ribber stitches knit plain stitches and the main bed stitches are selected with automatic patterning and are slipped to produce texture. It's the ribber stitches that will be the "right/public" side of the knitting.
In the main bed, selected needles (determined by the holes in a punchcard) will knit plain and non-selected (B position) needles will slip. When the same needles slip over several rows a ripple is produced in the fabric being created on the ribber.

Tips:

  • Because this is basically full-needle rib, use a fine yarn
  • Use a fine Fine Knit Bar to help the stitches knit properly
  • Set the ribber tension looser than the main bed to accentuate the ripple effect
Half Milano (Long Stitch)

slides.caption: A variation of Full Needle Rib, Long Stitch is the basis for a number of interesting ribber stitch pattern techniques.

Long Stitch (also known as Half Milano) is a variation of full needle rib. All needles on both beds are in work.
Cast on and establish for Full needle rib.

I've set my ribber carriage to slip in one direction. As I knit across, you'll see that the main bed stitches knit and the ribber stitches do not knit.

The ribber stitches slip.
Knit back and the needles on both beds knit.
Continue knitting, alternating knit on one bed and slip on the other. Slip - Knit - Slip - Knit Continue alternating slip in one direction and knit all needles in the other direction.
The side of the knitting where the rows were knit looks like stockinette.
The side of the knitting that had needles slip for one row, have stitches that are elongated.
You can slip on either the main bed or the ribber, just keep in mind which side you want to use as the public side of your knitting

Exercise #24 - Experiment with (learn) YOUR Carriage Settings
  1. Swing the ribber to "P"
  2. Pull every other needle to work
  3. Pass the carriage to align all needles in working position
  4. Pass the carriage and observe the action of the needles
  5. Set the ribber carriage to SLIP
  6. Pass the carriage and observe the action of the needles
  7. If your carriage has both left and right slip settings, repeat observing slip left only and slip right only

25
Exercise #25 - Put slip to work
Using Half circular ribbing, practice using slip with your ribber. Take it step-by-step and apply the settings to other ribber techniques
  1. Cast on for full needle rib
  2. Set the main bed to slip in one direction (left)
  3. Set the ribber to slip in the opposite direction (right)
  4. Knit left (only the ribber stitches knit)
  5. Knit right (only the main bed stitches knit)
  6. REVERSE the settings and repeat

26
Exercise #26- No pattern pintucks
  1. Setup and cast on for full needle rib
  2. Knit 10 rows
  3. Set the main bed to slip in both directions
  4. Knit 4-6 rows
  5. Cancel Slip
  6. Knit 10 rows
  7. Set the ribber to slip in both directions
  8. Knit 4-6 rows
  9. Cancel slip
  10. Knit 10 rows
  11. Repeat from to 3 times

Remember: Automatic patterning only controls the needles on the main bed.
But patterning can be combined with the ribber. Ribber needles remain in work, while slip (or tuck) takes place AT THE SAME TIME on the main bed.
